questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following best explain why the troposphere is described as the weather making layer?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The troposphere is the lowest layer of the atmosphere, about 8 km deep over the poles and about 16-18 km over the equator. It holds most of the mass of the atmosphere and almost all of its **water vapour, clouds and dust**. Heating from the ground, convection, evaporation and condensation all happen in this layer, so clouds, rain, wind, fog and storms (the weather) are produced there. Option B is the best statement: water vapour and the other gases absorb and redistribute heat and feed the processes that make weather. Option A describes a property of every layer, not the reason for weather; option C refers to the ozone layer, which is in the stratosphere; option D wrongly says that carbon dioxide and dust are small in quantity yet 'generate' heat.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: It contains gases and water vapour which regulate temperature
It contains the ozone gas that traps ultra-violet rays.
It has little quantities of carbon dioxide and dust which generate heat

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study Figure 1 on the general atmospheric circulation.

![fig-1](gce-al-geography-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

*Fig 1: Model of general atmospheric circulation. Source: Adapted from Complete Physical Geography (Nchangvi, 2020).*

Identify the air circulation model represented by X, Y, and Z respectively:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The tricellular model divides each hemisphere into three circulation cells. **X** lies between the equator (ITCZ, rising air and cumulonimbus clouds) and about 30 degrees N (subtropical high pressure): this is the thermally direct **Hadley cell**. **Y** lies between about 30 degrees and 60 degrees N, with the warm south-westerlies at the surface and the polar front at its poleward edge: this is the **Ferrel cell**. **Z** lies between about 60 degrees N and the North Pole, with the polar easterlies at the surface: this is the **Polar cell**. The sequence from the equator outwards is therefore Hadley, Ferrel, Polar, which is option B. Option D is wrong because the tricellular model is the whole system, not a single cell.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Ferrel cell, Hadley cell and Polar cell
Hadley cell, Ferrel cell and Polar cell
Polar cell, Ferrel cell and Hadley cell
Hadley cell, Ferrel cell, and Tricellular model

questions.enonce_markdown: It is a type of fog formed when warm air moves over a cold land or water surface.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Advection fog** forms when warm, moist air is carried horizontally (advected) over a colder land or sea surface. The air is cooled from below to its dew point and the water vapour condenses. Steam fog is the opposite situation (cold air over a warmer water surface); frontal fog forms near a warm front when rain falls into cooler air; inversion (radiation) fog forms on clear, calm nights when the ground loses heat by radiation.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 2 shows the distribution of a certain climate.

![fig-2](gce-al-geography-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)

*Fig 2: Areas of a given climate*

Identify the climate whose distribution is shown on figure 2.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The shaded areas on the map are the Amazon Basin, the Congo Basin and the Indo-Malaysian archipelago, all within about 5 to 10 degrees of the equator. These are the regions of the **equatorial climate**: high temperatures all year (about 26-28 degrees C), a very small annual range and heavy convectional rainfall (above 1500 mm) in all months. Tropical continental (savanna) and hot desert climates lie further from the equator, around 10-30 degrees; the tropical monsoon climate is found mainly in south and south-east Asia and West Africa coasts, not in the equatorial basins shown.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The data below compares the climates of two towns in Cameroon.

| Location | Mean Temp (°C) | Mean annual precipitation (mm) |
|---|---|---|
| Town X | 26.3°C | 4,230 |
| Town Y | 32.5°C | 900 |

Which statement best explains the climatic variation between the two towns?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Town X is cooler (26.3 degrees C) with a very high rainfall (4,230 mm); Town Y is much hotter (32.5 degrees C) and dry (900 mm). This contrasts a **coastal, windward** location, where moist south-westerly (monsoon) air from the Atlantic gives heavy rain and the sea moderates temperature, with an **inland (continental) location** far from the moisture source, with little rain, large heating by day and a high mean temperature. Option D is correct. A (same latitude) cannot explain such a contrast; B is contradicted by the data (the hotter town cannot be the one at higher altitude, since temperature falls with altitude); C is wrong because a lake near Town Y would raise rainfall and reduce the mean temperature, and being far inland would make the wet town drier, not wetter.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Town X and Y are located on the same latitude
Town X is located at a lower altitude and Y at a higher altitude
Town X is located far inland and Y near a large lake
Town X is located in coastal zone and Y far inland

questions.enonce_markdown: A measure of the atmosphere to remove water from the earth's surface assuming no limitation of water supply describes:
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Potential evapotranspiration (PET)** is the maximum amount of water that the atmosphere could remove, by evaporation and plant transpiration, from a surface if the water supply were unlimited. It depends on energy and atmospheric demand (temperature, wind, humidity). Actual evapotranspiration (B) is what really leaves the surface and is limited by the available water; evaporating pans (D) are instruments used to measure evaporation, not the concept itself.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which type of river regime is typical of rivers which flow in the Western Highlands of Cameroon?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the classification of river regimes used in Cameroon geography, a **simple regime** (one flood) is typical of the northern rivers with one rainy season, a **double regime** (two floods) of the equatorial south with two rainy seasons, and a **complex regime** of the rivers of the Western Highlands and the Adamawa, where relief, altitude and the two climatic influences combine to produce a more irregular hydrograph with a long high-water period and several fluctuations. The Western Highlands rivers (for example the Noun, the Mbam and the upper Sanaga tributaries) are therefore classed as complex. 'Tropical regime' is not one of the three regime types of this classification.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study Figure 3, which shows stages in the break-up of Pangaea.

![fig-3](gce-al-geography-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_3.png)

*Fig 3: Stages in the break-up of Pangaea.*

In which era of the geological timescale did Pangaea split into two main blocks?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The figure shows one supercontinent, Pangaea, about 225 million years ago, then two main blocks, **Laurasia** in the north and **Gondwana** in the south, about 150 million years ago. These dates fall in the **Mesozoic era** (about 252 to 66 million years ago, the age of the reptiles). The Paleozoic ended about 252 million years ago, before the split; the Cenozoic (since about 66 million years ago) is the era in which the continents moved to their present positions.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which crustal theory has as evidence the increasing ages of rocks on both sides of ridges and paleomagnetism?
questions.corrige_markdown:
At mid-oceanic ridges new basaltic crust is formed from rising magma and moves away on both sides. The rocks get **older with distance from the ridge**, and they record the reversals of the earth's magnetic field in symmetrical stripes on either side (paleomagnetism). These are the two main lines of evidence for **sea-floor spreading** (Hess, Vine and Matthews). Continental drift (Wegener) relied on the fit of the continents and fossil and rock similarities; isostasy is about the vertical balance of the crust; plate tectonics is the wider, later theory that includes sea-floor spreading, but the question names this specific hypothesis.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which type of volcano is formed at constructive plate margins?
questions.corrige_markdown:
At constructive (divergent) margins, such as the Mid-Atlantic Ridge (Iceland), plates move apart and fluid **basaltic lava** with low silica content wells up. It flows far before solidifying and builds broad, gently sloping **shield cones**. Composite cones are formed at destructive (subduction) margins from viscous andesitic lava and ash alternately; cumulo-domes (lava domes) come from very viscous acid lava; ash and cinder cones are small cones of loose fragments.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The Mindif, Rhumsiki and Kapsiki are all landforms in which of the following major relief regions of Cameroon?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Mindif, Rhumsiki and Kapsiki are rocky peaks, volcanic plugs and inselberg-like residual hills in the far north of Cameroon, on or near the **Mandara Mountains** (Mandara Highlands) on the border with Nigeria. The Western Highlands include Mount Cameroon, Mount Oku and the Bamenda and Bamileke highlands; the Coastal Lowlands lie along the Atlantic; the Northern Lowlands are the plains of the Benue and Lake Chad basin.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study Figure 4 below on weathering regions according to Peltier.

![fig-4](gce-al-geography-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_4.png)

*Fig. 4: Weathering regions according to Peltier. Source: Complete Physical Geography and Environmental Issues for Advanced Learners (Nchangvi, 2020).*

Using the graph above, what are the optimum conditions for intense chemical weathering?
questions.corrige_markdown:
On Peltier's graph the zone labelled **strong chemical weathering** occupies the lower left corner: high mean annual temperature (about 15 to 30 degrees C) combined with high mean annual rainfall (more than about 1500 mm). Moderate chemical weathering lies to the right of it and very slight weathering lies in the hot, dry area. Chemical reactions speed up with heat and need water. Option A and C include cold or dry conditions that fall in the mechanical, moderate or slight zones; option B limits rainfall to less than 1500 mm. Option D (warm to hot temperatures with rainfall above 1500 mm) is the one that fits the strong-chemical area.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: temperatures above -15° C and rainfall above 1000mm
temperatures above -5° C and rainfall below 1500 mm
temperatures above 0° C to 30° C and rainfall above 0mm
temperatures above 5° C to 30° C and rainfall above 1500 mm

questions.enonce_markdown: One of the following best explains why the lower course of a river is characterized by high deposition of sediments.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A river deposits its load when its **energy and velocity fall**. In the lower course the gradient is very gentle, the channel is wide and the river meets the sea or a lake, so the velocity decreases even though the discharge is large; the river can no longer carry all of its load (which is also very large because of the sediments received from upstream). Deposition then builds floodplains, levees and deltas. Statements A, B and D describe features of the lower course, or consequences of deposition, but only C gives the cause.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: A delta sometimes develops in the lower course
Rapids are rare in the lower course
The velocity of a river reduces in its lower course.
The valley of a river is widest in the lower course.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 5 shows the formation process of some coastal landforms:

![fig-5](gce-al-geography-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_5.png)

*Fig 5: Some coastal landforms*

Which of the following is a correct explanation for the formation of feature Y?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Fig. A shows a **wave-cut notch (X)** at the base of the cliff at high tide level, cut by hydraulic action and corrasion, and an overhang above it. When the overhang is no longer supported it collapses (Fig. B), leaving a vertical **steep cliff face (Y)** and a wave-cut platform exposed at low tide at its foot. The cliff then retreats. Option B describes headlands and bays, option C caves, and option D is wrong because a platform does not lower sea level or create a high cliff.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: wave erosion deepens a notch and eventually cause the overhang to collapse to form a steep face cliff
wave erosion erodes areas of less resistant rocks more rapidly to create bays or inlets
wave erosion through corrasion widens the weaknesses along coast lines to create caves
wave erosion widens and deepens a wave cut platform to reduce sea level and create high cliff

questions.enonce_markdown: In a field trip in a Highland area, students observed some portions with tree trunks, fences and telephone poles tilting downslope; and accumulation of soil at the foot of slopes. Which of the following types of mass movement is taking place?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The tilting of trees, fences and poles downslope and the accumulation of soil at the foot of the slope are classic signs of **soil creep**, the slowest form of mass movement: soil particles move a few millimetres a year by wetting and drying, heating and cooling and the action of roots and animals, so that objects fixed in the soil lean downhill. Rotational slip is a sudden, curved slide leaving a scar; mudflow is rapid and saturated; solifluction needs frozen (periglacial) ground.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A type of soil water that occupies the micro pores; less tightly held and so available for use by plants:
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Capillary water** is held by surface tension in the small (micro) pores between soil particles. It is held less tightly than hygroscopic water and is the main source of water available to plants. Gravitational water drains quickly through the large pores and is not retained; hygroscopic water forms a very thin film tightly bound to the soil particles and is unavailable to plants; field capacity is the amount of water a soil holds after the gravitational water has drained away, not a type of water.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Identify the correct pair of relief aspects that contribute to produce a soil catena (sequence of soils down a slope):

*Options as printed:* A) Gradient, high temperature, aspect   B) Drainage, gradient, parent material   C) Bedrock, slope steepness, aspect   D) Gradient, height of land, aspect
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **soil catena** is a sequence of different soils down a slope that is formed on the same parent material and climate. The differences are caused by relief: the **gradient** (slope steepness) controls erosion and the movement of water and material, **aspect** controls the heat and moisture received, and the **height or position on the slope** controls drainage, leaching and the deposition of material. Option D lists only relief aspects. Options A (temperature), B (parent material) and C (bedrock) each contain a factor that is not a relief aspect, but the question asks for a 'pair' while each option lists three items, so the best answer is not certain.

**Intended answer: D (Gradient, height of land, aspect).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: As a general rule, downward translocation would result in
questions.corrige_markdown:
Downward translocation (leaching or eluviation) happens where rainfall exceeds evapotranspiration: water moving down the profile carries soluble bases (calcium, magnesium, potassium, sodium) and nutrients out of the upper horizons. The surface soil becomes **acidic and infertile**. Duricrust and alkaline or neutral soils are linked to the opposite process, upward capillary movement of salts and bases in dry climates, where evaporation exceeds rainfall.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Development of duricrust on soil surface

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the pair that constitutes the relevant vegetation type and zonal soil type of the South Cameroon Low Plateau:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The South Cameroon Low Plateau lies in the equatorial zone with a hot, wet climate. Its natural vegetation is the **dense tropical rainforest** (equatorial forest) and its zonal soils are the deep red **ferrallitic soils** (ferralsols) formed by intense weathering and leaching. Savanna and tropical black earths belong to the drier zones of the north; mangrove forests grow on saline coastal mud, which is an azonal (intrazonal) soil and vegetation.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Isolate the ecosystem with the highest mean net production of energy, largest biomass and biodiversity:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **selva** (tropical rainforest of the Amazon type, or equatorial forest) has the highest net primary productivity of the major terrestrial ecosystems because of the year-round heat, light and rainfall. It also has the largest biomass and by far the greatest biodiversity. Savanna, taiga (cold coniferous forest) and steppe (temperate grassland) are all less productive and less diverse.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: It is a plant succession on a site that was previously inhabited by vegetation but the original vegetation has been destroyed:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **subsere** is a secondary succession: vegetation re-colonises a site where a previous plant community existed but was destroyed (by fire, farming, felling, flooding...). A prisere (primary succession) begins on a newly formed, bare surface such as lava or a sand dune. The climax community is the final stable stage; a plagioclimax (plagio-subclimax) is a community whose development is held at a stage by human activity.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In the management of ecosystems, priority should be given to the largest store of nutrients. Which management strategy is most appropriate for the conservation of the selva ecosystem?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the selva most nutrients are stored in the **biomass** (the trees) and the litter, not in the thin soil. Conservation therefore means protecting the trees, which is done by **creating forest reserves** (protected areas) and controlling logging and clearing. Contour ploughing, fertilisers and crop rotation are agricultural or soil conservation measures for cultivated land.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which is the main cause of urban floods in Cameroon?

*Options as printed:* A) Poor road maintenance   B) Frequent landslides   C) Poor drainage   D) Blockage of channels or culverts
questions.corrige_markdown:
Urban floods in Cameroonian towns such as Douala, Yaounde or Bamenda happen when heavy rainfall falls on built-up surfaces (impermeable roofs and roads) and the drainage network cannot carry the water. The most general cause is **poor or inadequate drainage**, which includes drains that are too small, poorly planned, unbuilt, or blocked by household waste and sediment, as well as building in wetlands and valley bottoms. Options C and D overlap (a blocked channel is one form of poor drainage), so the best answer cannot be established with certainty.

**Intended answer: C (Poor drainage).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Isolate a strategy to mitigate global warming.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Mitigation** means reducing the causes of global warming, that is, the emissions of greenhouse gases. Developing alternative (renewable, low-carbon) sources of energy such as solar, wind and hydroelectric power reduces the burning of fossil fuels. The other options (protecting low coasts, irrigation, using groundwater) are **adaptation** measures that help people cope with its effects, not strategies that reduce the warming itself.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: High use of underground water to solve water problems
Protecting low lying coasts from flooding.
High use of irrigation in dry areas

questions.enonce_markdown: Which is the most recent legislative action taken in Cameroon to fight pollution?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Cameroon has adopted legislation (in the early 2010s, with enforcement afterwards) banning the manufacture, import, possession and sale of **non-biodegradable plastic packaging and bags**, because plastic waste blocks drains and pollutes land and water. Water treatment and tree planting are management actions rather than legislation, and banning metals is not an anti-pollution law.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Banning the use of non-biodegradable plastics

questions.enonce_markdown: Which is the most populous country in the World today?
questions.corrige_markdown:
According to United Nations estimates, **India** overtook China in 2023 as the most populous country, and both have about 1.4 billion inhabitants. The United States (over 330 million) and Indonesia (about 275 to 280 million) are far behind. The answer depends on the date of the question ('today').

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A country with a population pyramid that has a triangular shape depicts:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A pyramid with a **wide base and a narrow top** (triangular) shows high birth rates, many children and a rapid fall of numbers with age because of high death rates: an **expanding (growing) population**, typical of developing countries like Cameroon. A stationary pyramid has nearly vertical sides (a rectangle), and regressive or declining pyramids have a narrow base because of falling birth rates.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
A given locality had a population of 200,000 in 2020, and recorded 23,400 births, 21,507 deaths, while 7000 people came in and 6,000 people travelled out of the area. What would be the growth rate given that population growth rate is

$$
\text{Growth Rate} = \frac{BR - DR + \text{Net Migration}}{\text{Total population}} \times \frac{100}{1}
$$
questions.corrige_markdown:
Natural increase = births - deaths = 23,400 - 21,507 = 1,893. Net migration = in-migrants - out-migrants = 7,000 - 6,000 = +1,000. Total change = 1,893 + 1,000 = 2,893.

Growth rate = $\dfrac{2{,}893}{200{,}000} \times 100 = 1.4465\% \approx 1.4\%$.

The trap is to ignore the migration (0.95 per cent) or to add all movements (7,000 + 6,000) instead of taking the net balance.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 6 shows a simplified version of the Demographic Transition Model

![fig-6](gce-al-geography-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_6.png)

*Figure 6: Simplified graph of Demographic Transition Model. Source: Adapted from Garrett Nagle (2000) Advanced Geography.*

Which of the following set of countries is likely to be in stage three of this model?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In stage three (late expanding) the death rate is already low and the birth rate is falling fast because of family planning, education, urbanisation and a lower infant mortality, so natural increase is slowing. Among the options, **China, India and Singapore** are the set usually given as examples of countries in or around this stage (falling birth rates, still growing populations). Mali is in stage two, Cameroon is in stage two (high birth rate), the United Kingdom and France are in stage four, and Spain, Japan and Sweden have very low birth rates and are in stage four or five (the stage five of the figure). The classification of countries depends on the source and the date, so the key is uncertain.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following aspects exhibits the highest selectivity in migration?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Migration is selective: some groups move more than others. **Age** is the most selective characteristic, since most migrants are young adults (about 15 to 35 years), who are the most mobile, seeking work, education or marriage; children and old people migrate much less. Marital status, occupation and ethnic group also show selectivity but to a lesser degree.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure7 shows the relationship between Population and Resources.

![fig-7](gce-al-geography-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_7.png)

*Fig. 7: Population/resource relationship*

Which of these letters best illustrates a theoretical situation where the quantity of resources matches the population of an area?
questions.corrige_markdown:
On the graph, GDP per head rises (increasing returns to scale) while the population is below the peak, which is **underpopulation**, then falls (decreasing returns) beyond the peak, which is **overpopulation**. The peak of the curve, at letter **B**, is the **optimum population**: the number of people that, with the available resources and technology, gives the highest standard of living (maximum output per head). At A there are too few people for the resources; at C there are too many; D is the point where the curve returns to the axis (very high overpopulation).

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is the main reason for high population density in the Western Highlands of Cameroon?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Western Highlands (Bamileke and Bamum country, the Grassfields) are among the most densely populated rural areas of Cameroon. Among the options, the main human and historical factor is the existence of **centralised chiefdoms** (fondoms and chefferies), which organised land, security and settlement, kept large populations together and encouraged intensive farming. The fertile volcanic soils and cool climate also help, but they are not options here. Industry is little developed in the region (A), hydromorphic soils are waterlogged and unattractive (B), and the relief is rugged and steep (D), which is a limit rather than an advantage.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Fig 8 below shows the Economic rent curve for 3 crops

![fig-8](gce-al-geography-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_8.png)

*Fig 8: Economic rent curve for 3 crops. Source: Nkemasong N et al (2009) Advanced Integrated Human Geography. P300*

What is the margin of transference from crop A to B
questions.corrige_markdown:
The margin of transference is the **distance from the market at which the economic rent of one crop equals that of the next**, so that land use changes from one crop to the other. Reading the graph, crop A has an economic rent of 30 (thousand francs) at the market and falls to 0 at 10 km, so its rent line is $ER_A = 30 - 3d$. Crop B has 20 at the market and falls to 0 at 40 km, so $ER_B = 20 - 0.5d$.

Setting $ER_A = ER_B$: $30 - 3d = 20 - 0.5d$, so $10 = 2.5d$ and $d = 4$ km (where the rent is 18,000 frs).

Crop A is grown within 4 km of the market and crop B beyond it. The 18,000 frs is the rent at the margin, not the distance.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The main focus of the Green Revolution was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Green Revolution (from the 1960s) introduced **high-yielding varieties** of wheat, rice and maize, together with fertilisers, pesticides and irrigation, to raise food production and **reduce hunger and famine in less developed countries** (India, Mexico, the Philippines...). It was not aimed at agribusiness profits, new foods or environmentally friendly fertilisers; the heavy use of chemicals was one of its criticisms.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: improving crop yields in commercial agribusiness corporations
inventing new forms of food to add variety to the human diet
reducing hunger and starvation in less-developed countries
encouraging the use of fertilizers less damaging to the environment

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study Fig 9, which shows how locational rent decreases with distance from the market. Why is point 'X' considered as the Break - even point?

![fig-9](gce-al-geography-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_9.png)

*Fig 9: Decrease in locational rent with distance*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Locational (economic) rent = total revenue - total cost (including transport). On the figure the rent line falls from 5,000 francs at the market to zero at **X** (beyond 10 km). At X the rent is zero, so **total revenue equals total cost**: the farmer makes neither profit nor loss. Beyond X the cost exceeds revenue (a loss) so cultivation of the crop stops, and X is the margin of cultivation (the break-even point).

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Total revenue is greater than total cost
Total revenue is less than total cost
Total revenue equal to total cost

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a non-renewable source of energy?
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Nuclear energy** depends on uranium, a finite mineral that is not replaced on a human timescale, so it is non-renewable. Solar energy, aeolian (wind) energy and biomass (wood, crop residues, biogas, which can be regrown) are renewable.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
What is the Beta Index (B) of the network illustrated in figure 10 below, where B=e/v?

![fig-10](gce-al-geography-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_10.png)

*Fig 10: Hypothetical transport network*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Count the vertices (nodes) and edges (links) in the network. There are **5 vertices** (four corners and the central node). The edges are: the four sides of the parallelogram (top, bottom, left, right) = 4, plus the two diagonals, each of which is split into two links by the central node = 4. So there are **8 edges**.

$$B = \frac{e}{v} = \frac{8}{5} = 1.6$$

A value above 1 shows a network with circuits. If the central node were wrongly ignored (7 edges), the result would be 1.4.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In transport studies, the term transhipment means:
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Transhipment** is the transfer of goods (or passengers) from one means of transport to another at an intermediate point, for example from ship to train or lorry at a port, or at a break of bulk point. Loading and unloading at a terminal (B) is a different operation, and the transfer from consignor to consignee (D) is the whole delivery of the consignment.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: The transfer of goods from one means of transport to another
The loading and unloading of goods at transport modes
The exchange of goods between carriers of the town
The transfer of goods from a consignor to a consignee.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Why are Cameroon's exports made up mostly of primary products?

*Options as printed:* A) Cameroon is a less developed country   B) Cameroon is a member of CEMAC   C) Colonial heritage   D) Her location in the tropics
questions.corrige_markdown:
Cameroon's exports are dominated by primary products (crude oil, timber, cocoa, coffee, cotton, bananas, rubber) mainly because it is a **less developed country** with a weak industrial base, little capital and technology for processing, so it exports raw materials and imports manufactured goods. The colonial heritage (an economy organised to export raw materials) is also a historical cause, and the tropical location explains the type of crops but not the lack of processing. Membership of CEMAC is not a cause. Options A and C overlap, so the best answer cannot be established with certainty.

**Intended answer: A (Cameroon is a less developed country).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The location of the cement factory in the town of Figuil in Cameroon is mainly because of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Cement is a weight-losing, raw-material-oriented industry: the main raw materials, **limestone and clay**, are bulky and expensive to transport. The Figuil factory in the North of Cameroon is located where limestone deposits are found. Industrial agglomeration, market and labour are not the main reasons for this location, and Figuil is in the Mayo-Louti area, not on the Diamare plain.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: The presence of other industries hence industrial agglomeration
The presence of raw material on the Diamare plain
Limestone and clay deposits in the area

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these factors constitute the strongest determinant of early settlement location?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Water is essential for drinking, cooking, farming and livestock, so early settlers chose sites with a reliable **water supply** (springs, rivers, wells), the strongest site factor for early settlements. Defence, fuel and the nature of the land were also important but were secondary to water.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following conditions would favour a dispersed rural settlement pattern?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Dispersed settlement (isolated farmsteads) is favoured by individual land ownership and the **absence of feudalism**, which allows each farmer to live on his own land, together with the availability of water everywhere and a peaceful environment. A point-bound resource (A), water at specific points (B) and the need for collective security (D) all make people cluster together, giving a nucleated settlement.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Exploitation of a point bound resource
Availability of water at specific points

questions.enonce_markdown:
Isolate the pair of factors which aptly explain why the differences between rural and urban settlements are becoming less clear:

i. Urban expansion and the incorporation of former villages into urban areas

ii. Countries maintain strict government definitions of what is rural and what is urban.

iii. Changing services and lifestyles in rural settlements

iv. Urban infrastructure is more sophisticated than rural settlements
questions.corrige_markdown:
The rural-urban distinction is becoming blurred because towns spread outwards and absorb surrounding villages (**i**) and because rural settlements are acquiring urban services, such as electricity, roads, telephones and shops, and urban lifestyles (**iii**). Statements ii and iv, in contrast, describe the maintenance of differences (strict definitions and more sophisticated urban infrastructure). The correct pair is therefore i) and iii), option D. (Option C is printed 'i) and ivi)', which is a misprint.)

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Fig 11 shows bid rent curves for some urban functions

![fig-11](gce-al-geography-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_11.png)

*Fig 11: Bid rent curves for some urban functions. Source: Nkemasong N et al (2009) Advanced Integrated Human Geography*

Identify the functions labelled A,B,C
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the bid rent theory, each function bids for land according to the profit it can make at each distance from the centre. **Commercial and retail uses** can pay the highest rents at the centre (accessibility) but their bid falls steeply with distance: this is the steepest curve and the zone A closest to the centre. **Industry** needs large sites and has a flatter bid curve, so it occupies the middle zone B. **Residential** use has the gentlest curve and takes the outer zone C where land is cheap. The order from the centre is therefore retail (commercial), industrial, residential, option B. Option C omits industry and option D gives the wrong order.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One of the deviations from zipf's model of city size distributions within a country or region holds that the largest city, often the capital, completely dominates a country's urban system both in terms of population size and function. Which of the following patterns suits the description above?
questions.corrige_markdown:
When one very large city dominates the urban system, many times bigger than the second city and with most of the functions, the distribution is called **primate** (the primary pattern). Examples are Paris in France, Lima in Peru, and (at national level) Yaounde and Douala in Cameroon to a lesser degree. The normal pattern follows the rank-size rule, the stepped order has groups of cities of equal size, and the binary pattern has two cities of very similar size dominating.

**Answer: C.**
themes: urban hierarchy and rank size rule

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study Fig 12, which shows Walter Christaller's Central Place Model.

![fig-12](gce-al-geography-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_12.png)

*Fig 12: Walter Christaller's Central Place Model*

Identify the K-value represented above..
questions.corrige_markdown:
In Christaller's central place theory the K-value is the number of lower-order settlements (including the central place itself) served by one higher-order central place. In the figure, each central place is at the centre of a hexagon and the lower-order places lie on its **six corners (vertices)**, each of which is shared by **three** hexagons. So each central place serves its own market area, plus 6 x 1/3 = 2 shares, which gives 1 + 2 = 3: **K = 3**, the marketing principle. K = 4 (transport principle) places lower-order centres at the middle of the sides, shared by two hexagons (1 + 6 x 1/2 = 4), and K = 7 (administrative principle) has six lower-order places wholly within the hexagon (1 + 6 = 7).

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following constitute the main factors for the rapid urbanization in Cameroon since 1960s?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Since independence the towns of Cameroon (Douala, Yaounde, Bafoussam, Garoua...) have grown mainly because of **rural-urban migration** (the push of rural poverty and the pull of jobs, services and amenities in towns) and the **natural increase** of the urban population, which is young and has a high birth rate. The other options are secondary or, for agricultural development, would tend to keep people in rural areas.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Rural-urban drift and natural increase in urban population
Historical factor and creation of schools

questions.enonce_markdown: Isolate the best and most current index in measuring the level of development between countries?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **Human Development Index (HDI)**, published by the UNDP, is a composite index of three dimensions: health (life expectancy at birth), education (mean and expected years of schooling) and standard of living (GNI per capita). It therefore measures development more fully than a single economic indicator such as per capita income or GNP (which ignore the distribution of wealth and social conditions).

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: All of the following factors have been responsible for globalization in recent decades. Isolate the most important factor.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Globalization is the growing worldwide integration of economies, societies and cultures. All the factors listed contributed, but the **advances in information and communication technologies** (internet, mobile telephones, satellites, electronic finance) are generally considered the most important, because they made instant communication and the global management of production, trade and finance possible; transnational corporations and cheaper transport used these advances. This is a judgement question, so the key rests on the usual textbook answer.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Growth of seasonal economic trading blocks
Advance in information and communication technologies
Development of modern and cheaper transport networks

questions.enonce_markdown: It is aid in the form of food, medicine and other basic necessities given to countries struck by a natural disaster:
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Humanitarian (emergency) aid** is the immediate help of food, medicine, shelter and other basic needs sent to people hit by a disaster such as an earthquake, flood, drought or war. Military aid concerns defence; project or technical aid finances development projects or provides experts; foreign aid is the general term covering all of them.

**Answer: B.**
